scientific_summary: The weak limits of rare pairwise-independent Bernoulli sums are exactly the nonnegative-integer laws with mean lambda and variance at most lambda. Every admissible law is realizable by exchangeable equal-marginal rows, showing that pairwise independence alone does not select the Poisson law of small numbers.
limitations: The theorem classifies scalar counts rather than point processes, does not treat higher-wise independence, and does not optimize support or entropy of the realizing rows. Equivalent coverage in older discrete-moment or finite-exchangeability literature remains a residual originality risk.
